newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The Central Electoral Bureau said 10.12 percent of 17.2 million eligible voters had cast ballots by 10 a.m.
The turnout was highest in the Transylvanian counties of Harghita with 20.15 percent, Covasna 14 percent and Mures 15 percent. In Bucharest the turnout was 11.9 percent.
* The Central Electoral Bureau reaffirmed that Romanian journalists are entitled to enter polling stations.
* Hungary's former Foreign Minister Geza Jeszenszky is in the Transylvanian county of Harghita representing foreign observers from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
* Some 48 percent of conscripts had cast votes by noon in 207 polling stations opened in the military units of the defence ministry.
* Since the opening of the polling stations no problems were reported at the government body in charge of organising the elections.

But local correspondents and the state news agency Rompres said some difficulties had occurred. In Gorj county, ink and stamps were insufficient, the logos of some parties were missing from ballot papers.
* President Ion Iliescu, candidate of the party of Social Democracy, said that it is very important for all voters to vote. He said he was confident in their choice.
* Emil Constantinescu of the Democratic Convention said after voting that each citizen had to make use of the power given him every four years.
* Petre Roman of the Social Democratic Union said he was confident and optimistic that today's vote would bring the change expected by voters.
* Nationalist Gheorghe Funar from the National Unity Party said after voting in Cluj that after the poll, Romanians would be more united and solve many problems.
* Gyorg Frunda of the Hungarian Democratic Union said after voting in Tirgu Mures that the construction of the next century would start after the elections and forecast victory for the opposition.
* Corneliu Vadim Tudor, said that huge amounts of money spent for the polls are not justified considering present living standards.
* Heart surgeon Ioan Pop de Popa said he entered politics to give an example to millions of undecided Romanians and appealed to them to vote.
* Tudor Mohora of the Socialist Party said he expected the poll to bring a radical change in politics.
* Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu said the next four years would be very important considering the new base to be used as a starting point.

* Virgil Magureanu, chief of the Romanian Intelligence Service, said the circumstances under which allegations surfaced about alleged collaboration of former French Defence Minister Charles Hernu with Romania's disbanded Securitate secret police were confusing and dubious.
He said that he no longer wanted to be SRI chief after the polls. -- Bucharest newsroom 40-1 3120264
